attractions.name: Apartheid Museum
attractions.summary: The story of apartheid and the struggle against it, told through film, photographs and personal accounts. Allow at least two to three hours.
attractions.label: Ormonde
attractions.street: Northern Parkway and Gold Reef Road

attractions.name: Constitution Hill
attractions.summary: A former prison complex where Nelson Mandela and Mahatma Gandhi were held, now home to the Constitutional Court. Guided tours run through the day.
attractions.label: Braamfontein

attractions.name: Vilakazi Street, Soweto
attractions.summary: The only street in the world where two Nobel Peace Prize winners lived: Nelson Mandela and Archbishop Desmond Tutu. Visit Mandela House and eat at one of the street's restaurants.
attractions.label: Orlando West, Soweto

attractions.name: Hector Pieterson Memorial and Museum
attractions.summary: A memorial to the students killed in the Soweto uprising of 16 June 1976, a short walk from Vilakazi Street.
attractions.label: Orlando West, Soweto

attractions.name: Cradle of Humankind
attractions.summary: A UNESCO World Heritage Site with some of the world's richest fossil finds of early humans. Visit the Maropeng visitor centre and the Sterkfontein Caves. Plan a full day.
attractions.label: About 50 km northwest of the city

attractions.name: Johannesburg Botanical Garden
attractions.summary: A large public garden with a rose garden, herb garden and walking paths beside Emmarentia Dam. Free to enter and good for a picnic.
attractions.label: Emmarentia

attractions.name: Origins Centre
attractions.summary: A museum at Wits University about the origins of modern humans, with a large collection of southern African rock art.
attractions.label: Braamfontein
attractions.street: University of the Witwatersrand, 1 Jan Smuts Avenue

attractions.name: Liliesleaf
attractions.summary: The farm that served as a secret base for the liberation movement in the 1960s. The 1963 police raid here led to the Rivonia Trial.
attractions.label: Rivonia

attractions.name: Mandela House
attractions.summary: Nelson Mandela's family home on Vilakazi Street, now a museum about his life and the Mandela family. Combine it with the Hector Pieterson Memorial nearby.
attractions.label: Orlando West, Soweto

attractions.name: Zoo Lake
attractions.summary: A public park with a lake, rowing boats, picnic lawns and a fountain, beside the Johannesburg Zoo. The Artists under the Sun art show is held here every month.
attractions.label: Parkview and Saxonwold
attractions.street: Corner of Jan Smuts Avenue and Westwold Street

attractions.name: Lion & Safari Park
attractions.summary: A wildlife park about 13 km from Lanseria Airport, with guided and self-drive game drives among lions, cheetahs and giraffes. Plan half a day.
attractions.label: Near Hartbeespoort, about 40 km north west of the city

attractions.name: Cedar Square
attractions.summary: A smaller shopping centre with shops, restaurants and everyday services.

attractions.name: Fourways Mall
attractions.summary: One of the largest shopping centres in South Africa, with shops, restaurants and a cinema.

attractions.name: Montecasino
attractions.summary: A casino and entertainment complex built to look like an Italian village, with theatres, cinemas, restaurants and a bird garden.

attractions.name: Nelson Mandela Square
attractions.summary: A paved square beside Sandton City with a bronze statue of Nelson Mandela, about 6 metres tall, and restaurants and cafés around its edge.

attractions.name: Sandton City
attractions.summary: A large shopping centre in Sandton, opened in 1973. A walkway links it to Nelson Mandela Square and the Sandton Gautrain station.
